title: Mix and solve
goal: I can pick a way to start a puzzle: draw it, list it or make a table. I can check and explain my answer.

learn.intro: Puzzles mix what you learned. Do not rush. Read it twice. Then draw it, list it or make a table.

example.problem: Siti's plant is 4 cm tall. It grows 3 cm every week. How tall is the plant after 6 weeks?
steps: Say what we know. It starts at 4 cm and grows 3 cm a week.
List it. Write 4 first. Then add 3 for each week.
The list is 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19, 22. Week 6 is the last number.
Check: 6 weeks of 3 cm is 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 18. Then 4 + 18 = 22.
example.answer: After 6 weeks the plant is 22 cm tall.

howto.title: How to start a puzzle
steps: Read it twice. What do I know? What must I find?
Draw it, list it or make a table.

try.text: A plant is 5 cm tall. It grows 2 cm every week. Write its height after each week in the tiles.
try.explanation: Add 2 each week: 5 + 2 = 7, 7 + 2 = 9, 9 + 2 = 11, 11 + 2 = 13. After 4 weeks the plant is 13 cm tall.

items.text: Find the rule. Write the missing number in the tile.
items.explanation: Each tile is 5 more than the one before: 7, 12, 17. So the missing tile is 17 + 5 = 22. Check: 22 + 5 = 27.

items.text: This pattern adds the same number each time. Write the missing numbers in the tiles.
items.explanation: From 3 to 7 is 4 more, so the rule is add 4. After 7 comes 11. After 11 comes 15. After 15 comes 19.

items.text: Fill in the missing numbers in the bonds.
items.explanation: 13 and 7 make 20, because 3 and 7 make 10. 6 and 4 make 10.

items.text: Fill in the missing numbers. Both sides must be equal.
Ravi has 70¢. He buys a drink for 45¢. How much money is left? {b}¢
Look at the graph. Fill in the blanks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Tuesday had {b} more cookies than Wednesday.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Monday and Thursday had {b} cookies altogether.

items.explanation: Tuesday has 9 cookies and Wednesday has 4. 9 - 4 = 5 more. Monday has 6 and Thursday has 7. 6 + 7 = 13.

items.text: Count the sides of all the shapes. How many sides are there altogether? {b} sides
items.explanation: A triangle has 3 sides and a square has 4 sides. 3 + 4 + 3 = 10.

items.text:
Lily is older than Ray. Jamie is younger than Ray. Amelia is older than Lily. Write the names, oldest first.
{ll}
items.explanation: Amelia is older than Lily, Lily is older than Ray, and Ray is older than Jamie. The order is Amelia, Lily, Ray, Jamie.

items.text: Circle the even numbers.   {circ:13|16|18|21|24}
items.explanation: An even number ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. 16, 18 and 24 are even. 13 and 21 end in 3 and 1: odd.

items.text:
Make 40¢ with exactly 3 coins. Use 5¢, 10¢, 20¢ or 50¢ coins.
{b}¢ + {b}¢ + {b}¢
items.explanation: 20¢ + 10¢ + 10¢ = 40¢. This is the only way: 50¢ is too big, and 5¢ coins would need 35¢ from 2 coins, which no 2 coins make.

items.text: Mei picks a secret number. She adds 7. She gets 15. What number did Mei pick? {b}
items.explanation: Go backwards. Undo adding 7 by taking away 7: 15 - 7 = 8. Check: 8 + 7 = 15.

items.text: Ben picks a secret number. He takes away 3. Then he adds 8. He gets 14. What number did Ben pick? {b}
items.explanation: Go backwards. Undo the last step: 14 - 8 = 6. Undo the first step: 6 + 3 = 9. Check: 9 - 3 = 6 and 6 + 8 = 14.

items.text: A ribbon is 13 cubes long. A string is 5 cubes shorter than the ribbon. How long is the string? {b} cubes
items.explanation: "Shorter than" means take away. 13 - 5 = 8. Check: 8 + 5 = 13.

items.text: The ruler shows a crayon. What is the crayon's length? {b} cm
items.explanation: The crayon starts at 2 and ends at 11. 11 - 2 = 9. Check: count 9 spaces.

items.text: Mei saves 5¢ on day 1, 10¢ on day 2 and 15¢ on day 3. The pattern keeps going.

parts.label: b
parts.text: After 4 days she has saved {b}¢ altogether.

items.hint: Fill in the table. Add each new amount to the total so far.
items.explanation: The amount grows by 5¢ each day: 5, 10, 15, 20. On day 4 she saves 20¢. Add each day to the total: 5 + 10 = 15, 15 + 15 = 30, 30 + 20 = 50.

items.text: Ravi puts 1 sticker on each side of 1 square and 2 triangles. Each sticker costs 5¢.
items.hint: Count the sides first. Then count in 5s.
items.explanation: A square has 4 sides and each triangle has 3: 4 + 3 + 3 = 10 sides. That is 10 stickers. Counting in 5s ten times gives 50, so the stickers cost 50¢.

items.text: Ali cuts 4 cubes off a rope, then 3 more cubes. He adds 2 cubes. The rope is now 11 cubes long. How long was it at first? {b} cubes
items.hint: Start at 11. Undo the last step first.
items.explanation: Go backwards. Undo adding 2: 11 - 2 = 9. Undo cutting off 3: 9 + 3 = 12. Undo cutting off 4: 12 + 4 = 16. Check: 16 - 4 = 12, 12 - 3 = 9, 9 + 2 = 11.

items.text: Mei folds a paper strip in half. 1 fold makes 2 equal parts. She folds again and again. Each new fold makes twice as many parts.
items.hint: Write the number of parts after each fold.
items.explanation: Parts after each fold: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. (a) 3 folds make 8 parts. (b) 5 folds make 32 parts. (c) 16 parts need 4 folds.

items.text: Aisha, Ben and Mei have 24 stickers altogether. Ben has 4 more than Aisha. Mei has 2 fewer than Ben.
items.hint: Guess Aisha's number. Does the total come to 24?
items.explanation: Try 6 for Aisha. Ben has 6 + 4 = 10. Mei has 10 - 2 = 8. Together 6 + 10 + 8 = 24. A smaller guess gives less than 24 and a greater guess gives more than 24.

items.text: Ravi has 3 triangles and some squares. He counts 17 sides altogether.
items.hint: Count the sides of the 3 triangles first.
items.explanation: A triangle has 3 sides: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. The squares have 17 - 9 = 8 sides. A square has 4 sides, and 4 + 4 = 8, so there are 2 squares.

items.text: What are the next 2 numbers? 8, 13, 18, 23, {b}, {b}
items.explanation: The rule is add 5. 23 + 5 = 28 and 28 + 5 = 33.

items.text: Fill in the missing number. 20 = 8 + {b}
items.explanation: 8 and 2 make 10, and 10 and 10 make 20. So 8 and 12 make 20.

Wei is taller than Siti. Ben is shorter than Siti. Who is the tallest?   {circ:Wei|Siti|Ben}
items.explanation: Wei is taller than Siti, and Siti is taller than Ben. So Wei is the tallest.
